class.name: Landscape3D
class.brief_description: A heightfield ground drawn as static chunk meshes with an LOD chain, made for path tracing.
class.description: Draws a height grid (from a [TerrainGenerator3D] or an [Image]) as square chunks of [member chunk_quads] quads. Each chunk has a chain of levels, every one half as dense as the one before, and the level is picked per chunk by projected error: the largest height gap between that level and full detail, in pixels at the chunk's distance, must stay under [member lod_error]. Neighbours are kept at most one level apart, and edges next to a coarser neighbour skip their odd vertices, so the ground has no cracks and needs no skirts. Vertices never move in the shader: a level change swaps the chunk's mesh. Under path tracing each mesh (chunk, level, edge variant) gets one acceleration structure, built when first drawn and kept, so a moving camera costs no rebuilds or refits; only level changes build. Levels depend on distance, not on view direction, so chunks behind the camera keep theirs and off-screen shadows and reflections see the same ground. Meshes no chunk uses are freed after about 600 frames. With a [TerrainGenerator3D] as [member source] and [member stream_heights] on, [method rebuild] first reads every 4th point only (a 4 m grid at 1 m spacing) and fills the rest by interpolation; the chunks the camera needs finer are read in full before the first frame where the 4 m grid would be clearly off, and all others on worker threads over the next frames, the ones the view needs first, nearest first. Until a chunk is read its errors are estimates calibrated on a sparse set of read chunks, it is drawn no finer than the 4 m grid, and its neighbours at most one level finer. Meshes for new levels are built on worker threads too, and a new set of levels is shown only once all its meshes are ready, so a frame never mixes levels that do not fit and moving costs the main thread well under a millisecond. Computing 1 m heights from the generator is the slow part (about 370 ns a point on four cores). A world that is loaded rather than generated should bake them once ([code]sample_heights(...).save_exr(path, true)[/code]) and set [member height_image] from the file: 4 km at 1 m then loads and shows its first frame in under a second. The node does not move the ground with its transform in sampling: with a [member source], keep the node at the world origin. The level-0 grid is held in memory; disk streaming comes later (docs/ideas/terrain.md). Collision: with [member collision_enabled], every chunk within [member collision_radius] of [member collision_target] (the camera when empty) gets a static heightfield body at full detail, whatever level it is drawn at, and loses it past 1.25 times the radius. With PhysX each cell is split along the same diagonal as the drawn full-detail mesh, so bodies rest on the triangles that are drawn (within a millimetre); other physics servers use their own split, up to the height difference across a cell off. A chunk still being streamed gets its body once read; the chunk under the target and its neighbours are read at once. At 1 m spacing and the default radius that is 49 bodies, built in under 2 ms, and a 64 m step costs about 0.3 ms. Bodies report this node as their collider.

method.name: clear
method.description: Frees the chunks, meshes and heights.

method.name: get_aabb
method.description: The bounds of the ground in the node's space.

method.name: get_chunk_edge_mask
method.description: The sides of [param chunk] stitched to a coarser neighbour: bit 0 toward -Z, 1 toward +X, 2 toward +Z, 3 toward -X.

method.name: get_cliff_point
method.description: Where the drawn surface lies over a point of the heightfield surface: the point itself, or pushed out of or into a steep face by [member cliff_relief]. For water laid on a face.

method.name: get_chunk_lod
method.description: The level [param chunk] draws now (0 is full detail).

method.name: get_chunk_lod_error
method.description: The largest height gap, in metres, between [param level] and full detail in [param chunk].

method.name: get_chunk_triangles
method.description: The triangles [param chunk] draws now, in global space, three points each. For tests.

method.name: get_height
method.description: The full-detail ground under [param global_position], bilinear between grid points.

method.name: get_lod_count
method.description: Levels in use: [member lod_levels], fewer if [member chunk_quads] is small.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: [code]chunks[/code], [code]triangles[/code] drawn, [code]chunks_per_level[/code], [code]meshes[/code] kept, total [code]mesh_builds[/code] and [code]lod_switches[/code], [code]build_msec[/code] of the last [method rebuild] (of it [code]source_msec[/code] reading heights and [code]measure_msec[/code] measuring errors), [code]update_usec[/code] of the last level pick (with any synchronous reads), [code]apply_usec[/code] to hand the last built meshes to the renderer, [code]unread_chunks[/code] and [code]chunks_streamed[/code] while streaming, the [code]detail_estimate[/code] added to unread chunks' errors (metres), [code]busy[/code] while worker threads are reading or building, [code]collision_tiles[/code] and the [code]collision_usec[/code] of the last collision update.

method.name: has_chunk_collision
method.description: Whether the chunk has a collision body now.

method.name: is_chunk_loaded
method.description: Whether the chunk's heights are read in full (always [code]true[/code] without streaming).

method.name: is_fully_loaded
method.description: Whether every chunk is read in full.

method.name: load_all_heights
method.description: Reads every chunk not read yet now, in parallel, and waits; for bakes, tests and captures that need the exact ground everywhere.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Reads the heights from [member source] or [member height_image], measures every chunk's level errors (in parallel) and creates the chunks. Returns [code]false[/code] when there are no heights.

method.name: update_collision
method.description: Adds and frees collision bodies for where [member collision_target] is now. The node does this every frame; call it after moving the target by hand within a frame, or in tests.

method.name: update_lods
method.description: Picks every chunk's level for a camera at [param camera_transform] with [param projection], on a viewport [param viewport_height] pixels tall, reads the chunks that view needs in full and builds the missing meshes, and waits, so the result is exact on return. Each frame the node does the same for the current camera without waiting (see [member stream_heights]); call this directly for tests, captures or other views.

method.name: update_lods_from_camera
method.description: [method update_lods] for [member camera], or the viewport's current camera (the editor's in the editor).

members.member: The camera that picks the levels. Empty: the viewport's current camera.

Metres of rock relief built into faces steeper than about 50 degrees near the camera: the finest level's triangles are refined there without cracks and pushed out into ledges of 3 m beds and staggered joint blocks. 0 turns it off.
Quads along a chunk's side at full detail (a power of two, 8 to 256).
Static heightfield bodies near [member collision_target]. Not built in the editor.
Physics layers the ground is on.
Chunks this close to the target (nearest point of the chunk, horizontally) get bodies.
The node the bodies follow, usually the player. Empty: the camera.
Heights as an image, one pixel per grid point from [member origin], used when [member source] is empty.
The largest height error a level may show, in pixels. 1 keeps the ground within a pixel of full detail.
Levels in each chunk's chain, full detail included.
The ground's material, for example a [TerrainMaterial3D].
World X and Z of the first grid point. Set from the source's rectangle when [member source] is used.
Friction and bounce of the ground bodies.
A node with [code]sample_heights(origin, spacing, size)[/code] and [code]get_world_rect()[/code], such as a [TerrainGenerator3D] after [method TerrainGenerator3D.generate].
Metres between grid points at full detail.

With a [TerrainGenerator3D] as [member source] (and [member lod_levels] above 3), read a 4 m grid first and the rest per chunk as the camera needs it, on worker threads. Off: [method rebuild] reads everything first. Reading stops (keeping what was read) when the generator starts a new [method TerrainGenerator3D.generate].
